model_annotation: Figure 10 is a grouped bar chart illustrating the “effect of context masking on case tasks” with results organized by language family and shown separately for two multilingual BERT models and two experimental conditions. The horizontal axis contains the categorical language-family labels in left-to-right order: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis is the value axis labeled “effect,” shown on a linear scale with gridlines and tick marks spanning roughly from 0 up to about 30 (with regularly spaced ticks at approximately 10-unit intervals). Each language-family category contains six adjacent bars (a grouped arrangement), with colors and labels given in the legend: mBERT-L₂ (dark blue), XLM-L₂ (light blue), mBERT-R₂ (green), XLM-R₂ (pale green), mBERT-B₂ (red), and XLM-RB₂ (dark red). Approximate bar heights by category are: IE-Baltic shows small values (about 2 for mBERT-L₂, ~4 for XLM-L₂, ~1 for mBERT-R₂, ~4–5 for XLM-R₂, and ~5–7 for the two red bars); IE-Germanic shows around ~10 (dark blue), ~1–2 (light blue), ~0 (green), ~2–3 (pale green), and ~14–16 (red/dark red); IE-Indic has the largest bars on the chart with green/pale-green around ~20–22 and red/dark-red around ~24–27, while the two blue bars are near ~0–1; IE-Romance has mid-range values with blues around ~5–7, greens around ~5–6, and reds around ~10–12; IE-Slavic family shows blues near ~9–10, greens around ~1–2, and reds around ~15–18; IE-other shows mostly small values with the red/dark-red bars around ~7–8 and the others near ~0–2; Isolate shows very small bars clustered near ~0–2 for all series; Semitic shows a tall dark-blue bar around ~16–17, light blue near ~0, greens around ~0–1, and reds around ~15–18; Uralic shows near-zero values for most series with a small dark-blue bar around ~2–3 and tiny others near ~0–1. All bars include vertical error bars (standard deviation as noted in the caption) with varying lengths, and the categories do not appear sorted by bar height; no bars are uniquely highlighted beyond their color coding and the error bars.
